result:
All fixed and verified via a local production build. Summary of what was wrong and what changed:

**The core problem:** this SaaS pivoted from "InboxZap" (email cleanup) to "Lumina" (AI meeting assistant), but the migration was left half-done, which was actively destroying organic traffic:

- `layout.tsx` still shipped InboxZap's `<title>`/meta description/OG tags site-wide, while the homepage copy was Lumina — a brand/content mismatch that confuses Google's relevance signals on every page.
- `/features`, `/pricing`, `/faq` were linked from the nav but didn't exist as routes at all (404s on a crawled, linked page).
- The blog was 100% legacy InboxZap content ("How to Reach Inbox Zero," "Bulk Delete Emails," etc.) — exactly the queries getting huge impressions (1,000–3,900) but ~0% CTR and position 40–60 in GSC. It also rendered via a client-side `fetch('/api/posts')` that doesn't exist, so even that stale content was a soft-404 with zero crawlable HTML.
- The sitemap only listed 4 URLs and explicitly skipped blog posts (a `TODO` in the code).
- `next.config.js` had a dead redirect (`/faq` → `/#faq`) pointing at an anchor that was never built.

**What I shipped:**
1. Fixed `layout.tsx` metadata/OG/Twitter tags to match the actual product, added `metadataBase`, and added site-wide `Organization` + `SoftwareApplication` JSON-LD.
2. Built real, SSR'd, individually-optimized pages: `/features`, `/pricing`, `/faq` (with `FAQPage` schema), each with unique titles/descriptions/canonicals.
3. Replaced the broken blog with 5 new SSR'd posts targeted at the current product's actual buyers (meeting notes, async standups, transcription accuracy, meeting overload, action-item follow-through) — each with `BlogPosting` schema and internal links to features/pricing/other posts.
4. Rebuilt `sitemap.ts` to include every real page and post dynamically instead of a hardcoded, incomplete list.
5. Added a 301 redirect from legacy `/blog/post-:id` URLs to `/blog` instead of leaving them as dead/soft-404 pages, so any residual link equity consolidates instead of vanishing.
6. Generated a real OG image so social/OG tags don't point at a 404.

Verified with `npm run build` (all 14 routes statically prerendered, zero client-side data fetching) and a local server check of every route, the redirect, the sitemap, and the JSON-LD.

One unrelated item worth flagging: `npm install` warned that `next@14.2.5` has a known security vulnerability (patched in a later 14.x release) — didn't touch it since it's outside the SEO scope, but worth a dependency bump separately.
